findings.title: WebKit seek can leave presented source time at the initial frame
findings.trigger: Run the existing isolated media test with ACANVAS_MEDIA_ENGINES=webkit; once readyState is at least 2, seek native video to 0.7 without a readiness grace delay.
findings.actual: After seek completion and a 10 second wait, native currentTime is 0.7 but published rvfc-observed presentedTime remains 0.
findings.impact: The saved presentation may describe the initial media position after the user has sought to a later frame; the required displayed-frame/time association is not established.
findings.sourceObservation: Frame callbacks publish metadata.mediaTime without a seek generation or callback freshness condition. The refresh path also publishes a sampled seek time. The exact overwrite order remains for the executor to instrument.
findings.acceptance: Correct the decoder/seek ordering with current-frame source authority; verify the failing WebKit flow repeatedly and preserve numbered-frame pixels and time precision in Chromium and Firefox.
findings.status: CLOSED after source fix and independent original WebKit plus three-engine video regressions
findings.closure: Source and seek generations invalidate old callbacks, seeking pauses pixel copying, seek completion uses explicit playback-sampled precision, and RVFC compositor submission timestamps reject stale frames. Independent original full WebKit flow passed without readiness grace; three-engine targeted regression retained actual initial RVFC callbacks and delivered them after seek.

findings.title: GIF descriptor limit is enforced after full parser allocation
findings.trigger: gifFixture with 50001 valid 1x1 frames, each color=1, left=0, top=0, width=1, height=1, disposal=1; call decodeGif on its ArrayBuffer

actual.result: GIF playback supports one to 10000 frames.

findings.impact: Small compressed input allocates all parsed descriptor objects before rejecting the documented frame limit; larger inputs inside the 20 MiB file limit can exhaust ordinary-client resources.
findings.acceptance: Bound GIF structural parsing before descriptor allocation, including frame count and malformed/truncated blocks; preserve current bounded composition/disposal/timeline behavior and verify the excessive-descriptor sample independently.
findings.closure: decodeGif scans byte extents, logical and patch dimensions, supported extension headers, terminated sub-blocks, 10000 image descriptors and 20000 parser records with cursor-only state before invoking parseGIF. Current composition/disposal/timeline logic is preserved.
